questions.q: A patient demonstrates the positive Froment's sign shown in the lower image. Weakness of which muscle is primarily being tested?
questions.explain: Froment's sign tests adductor pollicis, supplied by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve. Weakness causes the patient to compensate by flexing the thumb interphalangeal joint.
questions.alt: Two hand positions demonstrating negative and positive Froment's sign while holding a sheet of paper between the thumb and index finger.
questions.credit: Image: Athikhun.suw, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

questions.q: In a positive Froment's sign, the patient flexes the thumb interphalangeal joint to maintain grip on the paper. Which nerve supplies the compensating muscle responsible for this flexion?
options: Anterior interosseous branch of the median nerve
Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
Superficial branch of the radial nerve
questions.explain: Flexor pollicis longus flexes the thumb interphalangeal joint and is supplied by the anterior interosseous branch of the median nerve. Its action compensates for weak ulnar-innervated adductor pollicis.
questions.alt: Two hand positions demonstrating negative and positive Froment's sign while holding a sheet of paper between the thumb and index finger.
questions.credit: Image: Athikhun.suw, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.
